verdict.rationale: DBOS's own queue feature runs many workflows at once with managed concurrency and flow control, which delivers bulk processing of many items. However, nothing in the evidence shows first-class bulk management actions such as cancelling, resuming or forking many workflows in one operation; the Conductor API and dbosctl only describe per-workflow actions that a user would have to script. Missing for 10: documented bulk management operations over many workflows/items, examples of batch fan-out patterns, independent hands-on corroboration of bulk usage.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can perform bulk operations across many items at once

citations.quote: You can use queues to run many workflows at once with managed concurrency.
Queues provide _flow control_, letting you manage how many workflows run at once or how often workflows are started.
